name: CallRail
summary: Call tracking and attribution — which campaigns, keywords and ads produce phone calls and form leads. It is an attribution layer, not a phone system or CRM.
best_for: marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution
skip_if: you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight
honest_knock: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling — the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month (plus usage), or $50 a month billed yearly
pricing.notes: Four plans, read on callrail.com/pricing on 13 October 2026 in a live browser, each 'plus additional usage': Lead Tracking $55 a month, Lead Tracking Complete $105, Lead Conversion $165 and Lead Conversion Complete $215; on yearly billing the same four read $50, $95, $150 and $195 a month (the page states 'Save up to 10% with a yearly plan'). Every plan includes 5 local numbers, 250 local minutes and 25 text messages a month (texting only after the trial); the Complete plans add 1,000 form submissions. Usage past the allowance: extra local numbers $3 each, local minutes $0.06, toll-free numbers $5, toll-free minutes $0.08, texts $0.03, form submissions $0.02. API access is in every plan, free to 1,500 calls a month, then $80 a month (1,501-12,000) or $200 (12,001-300,000). Voice Assist (the AI answering agent) starts at $95 a month on top of Lead Tracking, plus $1 a call after 50 calls over 15 seconds. Users are unlimited on every plan. 14-day free trial, no card.
